## Reproduced source defect
Tested PR #166 head 2221e5e0bf312fe9ac44dc4b72345ce5f8e7e54a, package manifest 2026.10.20, Linux Node v24.19.0 with existing official @unbrained/pm-cli SDK 2026.10.17. This is a synthetic public-SDK source test, not npm-publication, CLI/tracker-generated-ID, or whole-project certification. Head rechecked unchanged immediately before filing.

## Source goal
[Uncertainty documentation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/2221e5e0bf312fe9ac44dc4b72345ce5f8e7e54a/docs/uncertainty-intervals.md) says items and dependencies are sorted and reordered source rows do not change samples. The [canonical feature](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/2221e5e0bf312fe9ac44dc4b72345ce5f8e7e54a/.agents/pm/features/pm-gantt-chart-uncertainty-intervals.toon) requires reproducible completion intervals. Public PmItem.id is a string; the runtime accepts both distinct IDs below (nonempty and under 128 characters).

## Reproduction
Run against the exact source, with the documented SDK dependency available:
```js
import { completionIntervals } from './index.ts';
const ids = [String.fromCodePoint(0xe9), 'e' + String.fromCodePoint(0x301)];
const items = ids.map(id => ({ id, title: id, status: 'open' }));
const options = {
  from: '2026-10-22', seed: 42, samples: 1000,
  estimates: Object.fromEntries(ids.map(id => [id, [480, 4800]]))
};
const a = completionIntervals(items, options);
const b = completionIntervals([...items].reverse(), options);
console.log(a.ok, b.ok, a.receipt.inputHash, b.receipt.inputHash);
console.log(a.items.find(x => x.id === ids[0]).completion);
console.log(b.items.find(x => x.id === ids[0]).completion);
```
The second ID is decomposed e plus U+0301. Both calls return ok:true. Actual hashes are bae3afb86ef0d9f8cf0f6e5b726c759a51156b8d758037ad9239c9bca0a745e1 and 7a629a1a72c6f05c29c03f6c3b6d753a0edaaed0ec8109432e69a98e15073e9f. For the composed ID, P50 changes from 5.4384443026501685 to 5.636664288816974 calendar days solely from row reversal.

## Cause and impact
[uncertainty.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/2221e5e0bf312fe9ac44dc4b72345ce5f8e7e54a/uncertainty.ts) sorts active IDs with localeCompare, which returns zero for these byte-distinct canonical-equivalent strings in this runtime. Stable sort therefore retains caller order, changing which task receives each seeded random stream and changing the claimed canonical input hash. This is not merely display ordering. Consumers feeding accepted external IDs through the exported SDK cannot rely on source-row invariance. No claim is made that ordinary generated tracker IDs hit this case; ordinary case-only pairs did not reproduce it. No data was lost or modified.

## Expected and acceptance criteria
- Define a deterministic total order for every distinct accepted ID, without silently merging normalized IDs.
- Reversing/reordering identical accepted inputs must preserve receipt hash and per-ID quantiles/sensitivity.
- Add composed/decomposed Unicode-ID regression plus ordinary ASCII controls; retain analytic distribution, unknown-propagation, bounded-work and replay tests.
- Verify built artifact when published; source success alone is not publication.

29 existing focused uncertainty assertions passed separately. This new equality assertion fails on the exact source; full build/typecheck/platform/packed CLI suites were not certified here. Deduplicated all 166 all-status repository issues/PRs, PR166 conversation and inline review comments, and the canonical feature before filing.

> 
> Added regression: `issue 167: composed and decomposed Unicode ids preserve per-ID quantiles when rows reverse`. It uses the issue's U+00E9 versus U+0065/U+0301 IDs, seed 42, 1000 samples and uniform 480..4800 minute estimates, plus an ASCII control. Both distinct IDs are retained, and per-ID quantiles, receipt hash and sensitivity remain identical under reversal.
> 
> Revert proof: restoring only the active-task sort to `localeCompare` makes this exact regression fail on per-ID completion equality; restoring code-unit ordering passes. `node test/revert-uncertainty.ts` caught all 7/7 behavioral reverts and restored the runtime files.

Validation covers this unreleased PR; no npm publication is claimed.
